intro: An action is a method of a regular service in your extension. With the default `Configuration/Services.yaml` of an extension, TYPO3 finds the attribute automatically, and you register nothing.

steps.title: Attribute
steps.text: Mark a public method with `#[AsAction]`, set its route and select a scope that exists, for example `content:read`.

steps.title: Typed input and output
steps.text: Typed parameters and an exact PHPDoc return type define the JSON Schema. TYPO3 validates the values and converts them.

steps.title: Declared errors
steps.text: Throw `NotFoundError` or `PermissionDeniedError` and declare each one with `@throws`. The exception code is part of the API, because the code sets the `type` of the error response.

results_intro: Without more code, TYPO3 makes both methods available in these channels:

results.value: Both operations with the `operationId`, parameters, response schemas and the documented `404`
`fetch_my_extension_news_latest` and `fetch_my_extension_news_by_uid`, for every client with the scope `content:read`
TYPO3 makes sure that `limit` is an integer and that the results match the declared array shapes

scope.title: Custom scopes
scope.text: The scopes of TYPO3 cover most cases. If an administrator must grant access to your actions separately, register a scope and reference its class in `scopes`.

options.title: Attribute options
options.intro: The attribute `#[AsAction]` also takes these options.

rows.text: The path below `/typo3/api/v<version>/`, for example `my-extension/news/{uid}`. A placeholder takes the value of the parameter with the same name. Actions of different types or versions can share a route, for example `GET` and `PATCH` on `records/{schema}/{identifier}`.

The identifier of the action. Without `id`, TYPO3 derives the identifier from the type, the route and the version, for example `fetch_my_extension_news_by_uid`, with the suffix `_v2` from version 2. The identifier is the `operationId` in OpenAPI and the name of the MCP tool. TYPO3 also uses the identifier in the registry of the actions and in `_meta`. Set `id` to keep the identifier when the route changes, or to replace a derived identifier with more than 64 characters.
The version in the path, by default `1`. An incompatible change becomes a new version of the same route, and the old version stays available.

A Unix timestamp. Responses send the header `Deprecation: @<timestamp>` (RFC 9745). OpenAPI marks the operation as deprecated, and the description of the MCP tool starts with “Deprecated since” and the date. TYPO3 sends no header `Sunset`, because the next major version removes the action, and the core does not know when an installation updates.

The channels of the action, by default all channels. `Target::backend` is the backend, `Target::http` is the HTTP API for apps of EXT:hub and the OpenAPI document, `Target::ai` is the MCP server. In a channel that is not a target, the HTTP API returns `404` and `tools/list` does not show the action.

A link from a `create` action to the action that fetches the new resource. The HTTP API then returns `201` with the header `Location`, OpenAPI documents the link, and the MCP tool result names the MCP tool and its arguments in `_meta`. TYPO3 sets the status and the header from the declaration, so the action cannot forget the header and the three channels always match. If a later version adds a link to an existing `create` action, the status of the action changes from `200` to `201`.

options.note: A `Link` points to the method of the target action, not to its identifier. The parameters are runtime expressions of OpenAPI, for example `$request.path.uid` for an argument or `$response.body#/uid` for a value of the result. TYPO3 checks the link when TYPO3 compiles the container.
